analysis:
Both units are base_text excerpts of docs/architecture/inference.md (lines 802-1209 and 1210-1635). The documentation-only PR changes head ranges 404-413 (a model-load eviction description) and 1095-1115 (new text on segmented paged admission, free 64 MiB segments parked per pool outside the grant, floor and ledger charge, and reinstalled at the next admission of the same size class). The patch excerpt is truncated, so the full new text for the parked-segment behavior is not visible. I found no code changes, no changes to the coordinator/provider wire contract, and no changes to the attestation or authorization controls.

Security-relevant observations for later passes:
- The new parked-segment description touches T-028 (residual GPU/KV data after a request completes) and T-041 (cross-tenant prefix cache). The visible patch says new segments wrap zero-fil..., which is cut off. If the corresponding code reinstalls released KV segments to a different request or account without zeroing, stale decrypted KV could cross tenants. This is documented only in the truncated excerpt, so I cannot confirm the behavior.
- The parked segments sit outside the memory grant, floor and ledger charge, so they may weaken the memory-accounting and availability assumptions. The text says they are released before a load or eviction (`releaseReclaimableMemoryForLoad`), which bounds that risk.
- The base excerpts I examined (GLM media, deadline admission, MTP, SSD prefix cache, calibration) are unchanged context and give no evidence of a regression. They do not contradict the T-041 posture: prefix reuse is salt-scoped, media requests are excluded from prefix lookup, and the SSD staging reservations are unchanged.

No finding is raised because the PR changes documentation only and the code-side behavior is not supplied. The next pass should verify whether the source implementing the segment parking zeroes or overwrites reinstalled segments, and whether it bounds them by `min(2 GiB, grant/8)`, as the doc describes.
